title: The Rise of Temujin
description: 1186-1206. Follow Temujin's unification of the Mongol tribes on the steppe: rescue his wife Borte from the Merkits, forge and then break the alliance with Jamukha, defeat the Naiman confederation, and be proclaimed Genghis Khan at the kurultai. The player begins with a small warband and must grow through raids, alliances, and decisive battles.

issues_found: Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization. The engine ships a Mongols civ (and Tatars/Huns as alternatives); leaving Temujin's own tribe as a random draw means his warband and any built architecture may be Frankish, Teutonic or Japanese, an entirely avoidable error.
SUBOTAI is placed in Temujin's starting warband dated 1186. Subutai was born c. 1175 and entered Temujin's service in the late 1190s; he did not ride with the Borjigin warband of 1186.

All four opponents — the Merkit, Jamukha's Jadaran, the 'Naiman-aligned outpost' and Tayang Khan's Naiman — are lumped into a single Player Two. The anda alliance and its rupture are handled only by CHANGE_OWNERSHIP, so the player never faces distinct tribal confederations as the history requires.

The Merkit/enemy camp is enclosed with PALISADE_WALL x8 and a GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH. Steppe nomad camps of the period were unwalled yurt encampments; the engine's yurts alone (already used) would have been correct.
Enemy chiefs (Merkit chief, Jamukha, Tayang Khan) are represented by KING units — dismounted sedentary monarchs for mounted steppe chieftains — when a renamed cavalry or Khan-type unit was available.

The war against Toghrul/Wang Khan of the Kereit (1203), the decisive campaign before the Naiman war, is entirely absent; the Kereit appear only as a passing text mention as allies, and the Tatar campaigns are omitted too.

The break with Jamukha is triggered by an invented event — raiding a 'Naiman-aligned outpost to prove your strength'. The historical rupture followed Dalan Balzhut and Jamukha's election as Gur-khan in 1201, not a scripted raid.

Victory is UNCONDITIONAL and fires on no condition, so the encoded goal is not the kurultai proclamation the objective text and history point to; nothing in the trigger graph makes winning depend on reaching the gathering ground or slaying Tayang Khan.

Victory condition is UNCONDITIONAL with no condition attached and fires immediately, so the scenario is won before the rescue of Borte, the anda with Jamukha, the Naiman war or the kurultai can occur; the encoded goal is nothing at all.

Both active players are assigned civilization RANDOM, so architecture, tech tree and unit skins may render as Franks, Japanese, Aztecs, etc., rather than Mongols/Tatars/Huns — an avoidable error given the engine ships steppe civilizations.

The Merkit, Jamukha's Jadaran and the Naiman confederation are all collapsed into a single player (TWO), so the three distinct steppe powers Temujin fought in sequence are indistinguishable, and Jamukha never actually exists as an allied faction (his warband is handed over by CHANGE_OWNERSHIP).

The Kereit under Toghrul (To'oril Khan) appear only in one narration line; their alliance and Temujin's decisive 1203 war against them — the pivotal step before the Naiman campaign — is entirely absent from the objective chain.

Jamukha's break with Temujin is invented as a consequence of raiding a 'Naiman-aligned outpost to the south'; the historical rupture followed the Dalan Baljut fighting and a dispute over pasture/succession, not a scripted raid.

Steppe chieftains (Merkit Chief, Jamukha, Tayang Khan) are represented by the KING unit — a functional stand-in, but an immobile-feeling European monarch is a weaker substitution than a renamed cavalry hero or cavalry archer would have been.
PALISADE_WALL and a GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH fortify a nomadic Merkit/Naiman camp; fixed fortification is out of character for 12th-century steppe encampments.
